Does exploring candidates with different chess features help a small AlphaZero-style agent find moves its own policy overlooked?

Local research prototype built on the ChessConceptDiscovery repository. Run laptop-main · generated 2026-09-17T18:47:55-04:00.

inconclusive

Plain-language question. At a fixed search budget, a chess agent usually spends its thinking time on the moves its network already likes. We asked whether deliberately spending part of that same budget on moves that are different in character (sacrifices, checks, promotions, king-side vs queen-side play) helps the agent find winning moves its policy initially ranked low.

Verdict. Observed difference +3.5 pp with 95% CI -1.5 to +8.8 pp; the interval contains zero.

1. What this study is and is not

This is a small, fully local, reproducible experiment about search-budget allocation. The "creativity" component under test is operationalised narrowly: discovering a useful solution that was initially unlikely under the agent's own policy. Success is judged by an exact forced-mate verifier, never by the network's own value head and never by an external engine.

Claim boundaries. No claim is made about novelty to humanity, artistic ability, subjective experience, or general creative intelligence. Novelty here is relative to the frozen network's initial policy only; withholding a task from training does not prove the underlying concept was absent from all training experience. This study does not demonstrate concept recombination. It does not reproduce DeepMind's models or results. The chess-feature distance used in condition 4 is the hypothesis being tested — it is not an established measure of creativity.

Splits are by source family (one random playout game or one endgame construction seed), never by adjacent row. Exact FEN duplicates and duplicate piece placements are removed globally before splitting. Board transformations are deliberately not applied because mirroring breaks castling and pawn-direction semantics; this leakage-detection limit is recorded in data_manifest.json. Every task stores the legal move sequence that produced it, so board.is_valid() is never used as a stand-in for reachability.

Checkpoint provenance

Training proceduresupervised tactical bootstrapping on exactly-verified forced-mate solutions, followed by an AlphaZero-style self-play/MCTS fine-tuning stage; this is NOT tabula-rasa AlphaZero training
Parameters5,576,661
Architecture{"trunk": "conv", "channels": 64, "blocks": 4, "policy_channels": 4, "value_hidden": 64, "obs_shape": [8, 8, 20], "num_actions": 20480, "encoding_version": "fromto-promo-v1", "obs_version": "obs-20plane-v1"}
Weights SHA-256f62131806f66ee904a69efcd2f27f3d1faf636865ce89466fe54ec8d03cfc01b
Bootstrap steps2580 gradient steps on the TRAIN split
Self-play240 self-play games, 3677 records
This is supervised tactical bootstrapping followed by an AlphaZero-style procedure, not tabula-rasa AlphaZero. The policy head was trained on root moves that the exact verifier proved winning on the TRAIN split; the value head received supervision only where the verifier returned a decisive, complete result. Positions with unknown game-theoretic value, and all truncated self-play games, carry a masked (zero-weight) value target rather than a fabricated draw label.

3. The four conditions

All conditions share the same frozen checkpoint, environment, legal action space, observation encoding and nominal simulation budget.

ConditionWhat it does
Standard PUCTOrdinary neural-guided MCTS. All 1024 simulations from the root; move chosen by root visit count. No diversity intervention.
Quality-onlyScreening search of 256 simulations, then the remaining budget split evenly over the top-4 candidates by screening visit share.
RandomSame screening and candidate count; the top screening move is kept as an anchor and the other 3 candidates are sampled uniformly from the eligible pool with recorded seeds.
Feature-diverseSame screening and candidate count; candidates chosen greedily to maximise normalised screening quality + 0.25 × minimum standardised feature distance to the already-selected candidates.

Eligible pool: every legal root move (cap 48, never binding on this benchmark), so low-prior alternatives are always reachable. Final move rule (identical for conditions 2–4): the candidate with the highest post-allocation root-player value estimate, tie-broken by visits then action id. Every candidate receives at least one simulation, so there are no unvisited candidates at selection time. Budget accounting: the screening search is run once per position, deep-copied for each condition, and its full simulation, network-evaluation and wall-time cost is charged to every condition that uses it. Feature computation time is measured and added to the feature-diverse condition even though it only reads already-produced states.

Recovery of initially overlooked solutions

Eligibility was fixed in the protocol before test scoring and is computed from the single common raw network policy, so every method is scored on the same 132 positions: a position is eligible when all verified solution moves fall outside the raw policy's top three legal moves.

What happened

The exact verifier proved 1 root move force mate in 2 (a6a2), checking every legal defensive reply. Feature-diverse allocation explored 4 candidates: Ra2+ (screen visits 176, 192 extra sims), Qe1+ (screen visits 18, 192 extra sims), Rh6 (screen visits 26, 192 extra sims), Rf6+ (screen visits 25, 192 extra sims). It selected a6a2, which the raw network policy ranked #5 with probability 0.054. The verifier says this move DOES force mate within 2. Standard PUCT selected a1b1 (raw policy rank #8, p=0.029); verifier: not a forced mate within horizon. Refutation of the standard choice: after Kb1 Black replies Kg2, which survives the 2-move horizon, so the mate claim fails. This shows the task objective was missed; it is not a proof that the move loses the game.

8. Stages, limitations and exclusions

StageStatusSecondsNote
hardware✗ not completed0.0completed
dependencies✗ not completed1.2completed
data✗ not completed393.8completed
model✗ not completed258.3completed
checks✗ not completed4.243 passed in 3.67s
calibration✗ not completed570.3completed
protocol✗ not completed0.0completed
evaluation✗ not completed3222.03000 rows over 200 test positions

Limitations

  • Benchmark scope. The tasks are short bounded forced mates with modest material. Performance here says nothing about general chess strength.
  • Model strength. The network is a small convolutional model trained for minutes on a laptop CPU with supervised tactical bootstrapping. It is weak, and both its policy ranks and value estimates should be read as model estimates only.
  • Observation is not fully Markov. The network input carries a single repetition bit and no move history. The search state keeps the full board with its move stack, so game rules are applied exactly, but the network cannot see history.
  • Feature space is a hypothesis. Distances between descriptors are not a validated measure of strategic difference, and a feature named sacrifice_proxy records an observed material deficit along a short line — it does not assert a sound sacrifice.
  • Leakage detection is partial. Near-duplicate removal is piece-placement based. Positions differing only in en-passant or halfmove counters are retained.
  • Statistical power. Confidence intervals resample 175 independent source families. With this many clusters the intervals are wide; read them, not the point estimates.
  • Excluded / anomalous rows. Illegal selected moves: 0. Rows whose oracle status was not ok: 0 (such tasks are filtered out at generation time and excluded from verified scoring).

9. Reproduce this run

git clone https://github.com/jaycewalzer1/ChessConceptDiscovery
cd ChessConceptDiscovery
python -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

# smoke test (about a minute)
python -m scripts.run_experiment --profile smoke --seed 42

# the run shown in this report
python -m scripts.run_experiment --profile laptop --max-minutes 120 --seed 42 --run-id laptop-main

# resume an interrupted laptop run
python -m scripts.run_experiment --profile laptop --resume --output-dir outputs/laptop-main

Artifacts for this run live in outputs/laptop-main/: protocol.json, hardware.json, data_manifest.json, training_summary.json, checkpoint_metadata.json, results.jsonl, summary.json, report.md, report.html, case_studies.html, examples.pgn, figures/, case_studies/, logs/.

10. Related work

This prototype is a small local study inspired by two published lines of work, which it does not reproduce:

  • Schut et al., Bridging the Human–AI Knowledge Gap: Concept Discovery and Transfer in AlphaZero, arXiv:2310.16410.
  • Zahavy et al., Diversifying AI: Towards Creative Chess with AlphaZero, arXiv:2308.09175.

Related work was identified from the two references supplied with the task: Schut et al., 'Bridging the Human-AI Knowledge Gap' (arXiv:2310.16410), which extracts concepts an AlphaZero-style chess agent has learned; and Zahavy et al., 'Diversifying AI' (arXiv:2308.09175), which trains a population of diverse chess agents. No systematic literature search was performed in this session, and no claim beyond the titles and general subject matter of those two papers is asserted here.
